title: 12-Bar Shuffle in A
summary: The form every jam session knows. Drill the boogie shuffle riff, then connect the minor pentatonic boxes and learn when to switch to the major pentatonic.
skills: The boogie as a pedal tone, with a stretch
notes: Generic blues form. All parts are original practice material.

lessons.title: Feel the shuffle
lessons.goal: Play the boogie riff with a lazy, swung eighth note.
body: Shuffle eighths are long-short, like a triplet with the middle note left out. Say "HUMP-ty DUMP-ty" in time with the hi-hat.
The riff is a two-note power chord where the top note rocks between the fifth and sixth. On A it's the open A string; on D, the D string or 5th fret of the A; on E, the open low E.
steps: Play along with the boogie shuffle at 80 bpm, palm-muting lightly.
Mute rhythm guitar and keep it going through all twelve bars.

lessons.title: Know where you are in the twelve bars
lessons.goal: Call out every chord change before it happens.
body: This chorus uses a quick change: bar 2 goes to D7 and back. Then four bars of A, two of D, two of A, and the turnaround: E7, D7, A7, E7.
Watch the arrangement strip under the fretboard and say the next chord out loud a bar early.
steps: Play the seventh-chord stabs on 2 and 4.
Turn the stabs off and play them with your eyes off the screen.

lessons.title: Box 1 and its neighbours
lessons.goal: Play A minor pentatonic box 1 at the 5th fret, then connect to box 2.
body: Box 1 is the shape you know, root on the 5th fret of the low E. Box 2 starts on the C at the 8th fret and overlaps box 1 by a whole column of notes.
Use the shared notes as bridges: slide from the 7th to the 9th fret on the G string to move up a box.
steps: Loop the box 1 lick and learn it.
Switch the fretboard to position 2 and find the same notes there.
Improvise using only the notes both boxes share, then spread out.

lessons.title: Sweet side, sour side
lessons.goal: Hear the difference between major and minor pentatonic over A7.
body: Minor pentatonic has a C, which rubs against the C# in A7. That bluesy rub is the sour side. Major pentatonic uses C# instead and sounds sweet and country-ish.
Shortcut: the A major pentatonic box is the A minor box slid down three frets, to the 2nd fret.
steps: Play the major pentatonic lick and compare it to the box 1 lick.
Over A7 try major, over D7 and E7 try minor, and listen to the switch.

lessons.title: Stretch from a pedal tone
lessons.goal: Hold the root with your index finger and stretch the boogie up the neck.
body: The boogie riff is a pedal tone: the open A string keeps ringing while the 5th and 6th move above it. Up the neck there's no open string to do that, so a finger has to hold the root.

Your index finger holds the root, your ring finger plays the 5th two frets higher, and your little finger stretches to the 6th, four frets from your index. That stretch is the exercise. Over D7 the shape moves to the A string and your hand stays at the 5th fret; over E7 it slides up two frets.
steps: Listen with the neck on Fingers. Your index finger (the ringed dot) never lifts during a chord.
Mute the lead part and play it at 80 with the shuffle. Keep your index finger flat on the root and let your little finger reach.
If the stretch hurts, stop and come back to it later. Your reach grows over days of short practice, not in one long session.
When it's comfortable, play the root and the upper note one after the other instead of together, and listen to the root keep ringing under the moving note.

lessons.title: Boogie-woogie left hand
lessons.goal: Walk the boogie line in the left hand through all twelve bars.
body: Root, third, fifth, sixth, flat seventh, and back down, swung. It's the same line the bass plays, and it moves to D and E with the chords.
The right hand only stabs on beats 2 and 4, so you can focus on the left.
steps: Left hand alone over A for a few minutes.
Follow the changes to D and E.

lessons.title: Shuffle and the turnaround
lessons.goal: Hear how a fill marks the end of the twelve bars.
body: The shuffle swings the hi-hat's offbeats late. In the last bar the hats stop and the snare plays a short roll, and a crash marks the top of the next chorus. Drummers use fills like this to keep the band in the form.
steps: Solo drums with the turnaround fill and count the bars.
In Capture, set 2 bars and build a fill for bars 11 and 12.
